_note: Timed against the scene windows the film actually uses: s1 0-28s, s2 28-40, s3 40-65, s4 65-82, s5 82-102, s6 102-120, s7 120-145, s8 145-165, s9 165-190. A line must FINISH inside its scene, so each is budgeted at roughly 14 characters per second — this voice's real pace, measured. atMs is the earliest a line may start; build-narration.ps1 pushes it later if the previous line is still going, and reports the push. If you see a push larger than about 300ms, the line before it is too long for its window: shorten it rather than moving the mark.

lines.text: Somebody books the thing. Four bus tickets to Goa.
Nine thousand six hundred rupees, on one card.
One friend pays. One says tonight. One says tomorrow.
One starts typing, and stops.
Eleven days later, she is still asking.
What if nobody had to pay first?
Sutra is a payment protocol for more than one person.
The same trip, done properly.
Everyone gets their own link, and their own share.
They approve on their own card, capped at their own number.
And approving charges nothing at all.
Only when the last person is in does every card get charged.
A split can start anywhere. Say it in a sentence.
It finds real places from OpenStreetMap.
Paste a link. It reads the merchant's own price.
Photograph a bill. Every line, checked against the total.
Planning is the part that isn't about money.
Everyone says when they're free, and what they can spend.
It ranks real venues, and always says why.
Budgets stay private.
Every group has a thread. Tag the agent in it.
It answers from real state. It chases people for you.
And it always refuses to move money.
That needs your own passkey.
This runs inside NANDA Town, as a real payments plugin.
The bundled one pools money into the organiser's balance.
Ours never pools.
Four cards pay a merchant outside the simulator.
One agent structurally cannot pay another.
Now the part most demos leave out. Where this stops.
A shared cart is paid by several cards.
Most checkouts have one card field.
So sutra collects the money. It does not place that order.
It finishes end to end when everyone buys their own item.
And at a venue, where a table hands over four cards.
Every group ends in a signed receipt.
It never claims a charge it did not make.
Nothing pooled. Nothing fronted. Nothing invented.
